newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat up on reported Iranian purchase.
newsitem.headline: French wheat up on reported Iranian purchase.

text.p: French wheat prices firmed on Friday after Iran apparently bought between 200,000 and 400,000 tonnes of French wheat, traders said.
There was no official confirmation of the deal.
Traders cited selling prices ranging from $139 to $144 per tonne, Fob.
"It is an unusually high tonnage for that country," one dealer said.
Rouen wheat for February was bid at 857.50 francs per tonne, up 2.50 francs from Thursday, while April delivery firmed five francs at 850 francs per tonne. Both exclude carrying charges.
Dealers largely ignored the outcome of Thursday's EU grain auction, saying the wheat rebate was in line with world prices and a firmer dollar.
But they said tonnages granted were still too low to allow the European Union to export its large crop surplus.
"The tonnage awarded is not realistic when compared to the EU's export goal," one dealer said

On Thursday the European Union released 115,000 tonnes of soft wheat at a maximum refund of 17.99 Ecus per tonne, one Ecu less than the previous week. The award valued a tonne of late February French wheat at around $143 and March $1-2 less.
The EU also granted 180,000 tonnes of barley at a rebate of 27.94 Ecus per tonne.
Barley prices were steady on Thursday at 852.50-855 francs per tonne.
